newsitem.title: USA: Albright to maintain tough U.S. Cuba policy.
newsitem.headline: Albright to maintain tough U.S. Cuba policy.

text.p: Secretary of State Madeleine Albright said on Friday Washington would maintain its tough isolationist policy on Cuba and said it was a mistake to have a "romantic view" of communist leader Fidel Castro.

Albright, speaking at her first news conference a day after being sworn in to office, said: "Cuba is an embarrassment to the Western Hemisphere and I think we need to keep making clear that there needs to be a change there."
Albright said Castro was "a dictator who runs his country in the way dictators did in the '50s and '60s" and added: "I believe it is a mistake to have a romantic view of Fidel Castro."

Her comments appeared aimed at Canada, whose foreign minister Lloyd Axworthy met with Castro on Wednesday in Havana and reached agreement to work together on a range of issues, including economic cooperation and human rights.
Albright did note that human rights had been part of the Canadian-Cuban discussions. Washington is engaged in an intiative to persuade its allies to press Havana more forcefully on that issue.

Albright indicated that U.S. disagreement with Canada over Axworthy's visit would not damage relations with its northern neighbour. "We have the best possible relations with Canada," she said, adding: "We expect to continue to have very good relations."
